elements.name: Client application
elements.description: Any program that speaks the Postgres wire protocol. Its startup user name selects its tenant.

elements.name: Operator
elements.description: Runs proxy instances, writes the static fleet config, reads health and stats, drains an instance with SIGTERM.

elements.name: Developer or reader
elements.description: Runs simulator scenarios from a seed, replays a failure from its printed REPLAY line, runs make test / chaos / bench.

elements.name: mini-gateway
elements.description: A proxy that speaks the Postgres wire protocol (simple-query subset) in front of one Postgres: a hard-capped connection pool lent per transaction, per-tenant admission with two CoDel modes, read coalescing, an off-by-default retry policy, snapshot observability. Terminates client TLS; logs clients in with SCRAM-SHA-256. Runs as N independent instances.

elements.name: Postgres
elements.description: One ordinary Postgres server. Sees at most the fleet's connection budget, all logged in as one role.

elements.name: Metrics and log readers
elements.description: Everything that reads what the adapters produce: a Prometheus fed through an OpenTelemetry Collector or by direct scrape, flushed CSV files read by tests and DuckDB, log readers. They merge across instances; no component knows about them. The observability component view shows them one by one.

elements.name: Flushed CSV files
elements.description: One directory per run on local disk: run.csv, metrics.csv, histograms.csv, schema version 1 (PLAN.md section 7.7; columns in docs/csv-schema.md). Same columns in every flush; every tenant has its own rows; run.csv is written last, so a run without it did not finish. Nothing has to be running to read them.

elements.name: DuckDB (analysis tool)
elements.description: The DuckDB command-line tool (version family 1.5.x), run after a run by scripts/csv-assert.sh and by hand. Reads the flushed files with read_csv and runs SQL over them. Never imported, linked or started by the proxy.

elements.name: OpenTelemetry Collector
elements.description: Receives the proxy's OTLP/HTTP push, batches it and exposes the metrics on a Prometheus endpoint. Dev setup: docker-compose in deploy/obs-dev (chunk 15).

elements.name: Prometheus
elements.description: End of the production path. Scrapes the Collector; sees low-cardinality labels and the bounded tenant label only. Fleet totals are sums over the instance label.

elements.name: pgproto3 (from pgx/v5)
elements.description: Go package github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgproto3: Postgres wire message structs with Encode and Decode. The one external dependency, used for message encoding only.

elements.name: Shell and binary
elements.description: cmd/mini-gateway and internal/shell. Listeners, one reader and one writer goroutine per connection, bounded mailboxes, a deadline on every socket operation, TLS on both legs with crypto/tls (it answers a client's TLS request, upgrades the socket and buffers nothing across the upgrade), the admin listener on its own port, signal handling. Makes no decisions: it posts events to the engine and performs the actions the engine returns.

elements.name: Shell and binary
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-shell`.

elements.name: Engine
elements.description: internal/proxy. One single-threaded, sans-I/O state machine per instance: events in, actions out. Holds the client and database connection tables and the request pipeline with its stage seams. The simulator and the shell drive this same code.

elements.name: Engine
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-engine`.

elements.name: Wire layer
elements.description: internal/pgwire. Everything that knows Postgres: framing, both session state machines, the query-cycle tracker, the SQL lexer, the statement classifier with its courtesy reject list, the safe-shape recogniser that decides sharing, the error contract, the wire snapshot. The only product package allowed to import pgproto3. Its test packages pgwiretest, wireworld and clsworld run this code in the simulator.
plannedNotes: Built in chunks 4 and 5 (internal/pgwire): every component drawn here except the codec boundary. Chunk 4: the framer, the hand-written message coding, both session machines, the SCRAM-SHA-256 functions, the two trackers, the startup FATAL replies, the wire snapshot, and the test packages pgwiretest and wireworld. Chunk 5: the SQL lexer, the reject list, the statement classifier, the safe-shape recogniser, the error table with its reply builders, and the test package clsworld. Not built: the codec boundary (no file in the package imports pgproto3; the reply builders code their messages by hand). No engine exists yet, so only the test proxies drive this code, and nothing produces outcomes.

elements.name: Wire layer
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-pgwire`.

elements.name: Work vocabulary
elements.description: internal/work. Small plain types the cores are written against: tenant, unit of work with its class, reject reason and sharing flags, share key and its scope, outcome, refusal. Carries no Postgres type and imports only the standard library. This is the extension seam for a second protocol.

elements.name: Work vocabulary
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-work`.

elements.name: Admission
elements.description: internal/admission. Rate gate, per-tenant queues with two selectable queue rules, adaptive LIFO, round-robin dispatcher with shares that bind under saturation, adaptive concurrency limit.

elements.name: Admission
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-adm`.

elements.name: Pool
elements.description: internal/pool. Hard-capped database connections, creation limiter, leases per transaction, the one breaker, the dirty-connection table.

elements.name: Pool
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-pool`.

elements.name: Coalescer
elements.description: internal/coalesce. Identical statements share one database read: in auto mode those the wire layer marks as fitting the safe shape, in hinted mode those carrying the client's mark. Never writes.

elements.name: Coalescer
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-coal`.

elements.name: Retry policy
elements.description: internal/retry. A policy interface. Off by default; the other policy retries once, only when nothing reached the database, within a 10% budget.

elements.name: Retry policy
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-retry`.

elements.name: Observability
elements.description: internal/obs and its sub-packages; test/analysis; scripts/csv-assert.sh. Snapshot conventions (the one raw export), integer histogram, metric registry, collector, the adapter interface and its adapters (Prometheus text, JSON, CSV flush, log line, OTLP push), fleet merge, health, and the SQL assertions over flushed files.
plannedNotes: Built in chunks 1, 3, 4 and 5: everything except the OTLP push adapter (chunk 15) and the health rules that read other components (chunk 6 on). No engine or shell exists yet, so only the simulator's scenario harness (internal/obs/simrun) creates a collector, and nothing serves the outputs over HTTP.

No engine or shell exists yet, so only the simulator's scenario harness (internal/obs/simrun) creates a collector, and nothing serves the outputs over HTTP.

elements.name: Configuration
elements.description: internal/config. The config file, the static fleet block (instance count N; fleet budgets divided by N), and load-time validation that fails closed.

elements.name: Configuration
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-config`.

elements.name: Simulator harness
elements.description: internal/sim and its sub-packages simnet, simtls, fakepg, workload, world, simtest and simtoy; internal/testclient; internal/randdist; cmd/mgsim; scripts/tier-r.sh. A deterministic single-threaded world: virtual clock, simulated byte streams, a simulated TLS handshake, a fake Postgres, simulated clients, scenarios with a driver interface, faults, replay. Its fake Postgres is checked against a real Postgres 17. Test code; built before any proxy code.
plannedNotes: Built in chunks 1, 2 and 4: every component drawn here — the kernel (internal/sim), simnet, simtest, the toy protocol (simtoy), cmd/mgsim, the fake Postgres, the simulated clients, the test client, the simulated TLS handshake (simtls), the scenario world with its five direct baselines (clients straight at the fake, no proxy) and the fidelity runner, and scripts/tier-r.sh. Not built: no engine exists yet, so the harness drives the fake Postgres, the toy protocol and the wire layer's two test proxies (startup-only, and the classifier scenarios' gateway); nothing implements the engine's transport seam, and no synthetic workload drives the cores.

elements.name: Simulator harness
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-sim`.
plannedNotes: Built in chunks 1, 2 and 4: every component drawn here — the kernel (internal/sim), simnet, simtest, the toy protocol (simtoy), cmd/mgsim, the fake Postgres, the simulated clients, the test client, the simulated TLS handshake (simtls), the scenario world with its five direct baselines (clients straight at the fake, no proxy) and the fidelity runner, and scripts/tier-r.sh. Not built: no engine exists yet, so the harness drives the fake Postgres, the toy protocol and the wire layer's two test proxies (startup-only, and the classifier scenarios' gateway); nothing implements the engine's transport seam, and no synthetic workload drives the cores.

elements.name: End-to-end suite and load generator
elements.description: test/e2e and cmd/loadgen. Each scenario is written once and runs on the simulator (tier S) and on the real binary against a real Postgres (tier R). The load generator is open-loop.

elements.name: End-to-end suite and load generator
elements.description: Neighbour in a component view: stands for the container `c-e2e`.

elements.name: Transport seam
elements.description: Dialer and byte-stream connection events and actions: open, bytes in, bytes out, closed. Knows no protocol. Two implementations: TCP in the shell, simulated streams in the harness.

elements.name: Client session table
elements.description: One entry per client connection: its wire state machine, tenant, transaction state, the single request it may have inside the proxy, and its bounded reply buffer.

elements.name: Database connection table
elements.description: One entry per database connection: its wire state machine, the query-cycle tracker, and who holds it.

elements.name: Request pipeline
elements.description: The fixed order every request takes, each stage a small interface: classify, reject list, draining, breaker, rate gate, coalesce, queue, lease, forward, release. Statements inside an open transaction skip from classify straight to forward on the connection the client already holds.

elements.name: Reply relay
elements.description: Streams database messages to the client (or to every waiter of a shared read) through bounded buffers, with back pressure in both directions. Never sends a short reply that looks complete.

elements.name: Failure classifier
elements.description: For every failure records whether any byte reached the database, and picks the error-contract row.

elements.name: Deadline table
elements.description: Every wait in the timeout budget, as deadlines on the injected clock; returns the next wake-up time as an action.

elements.name: Drain controller
elements.description: Sequences shutdown: stop admitting, finish transactions in progress within a bound, close idle connections, exit.

elements.name: Snapshot publisher
elements.description: Collects every component's Snapshot() between events and hands the copy to the collector.

elements.name: Framer
elements.description: Ours. Cuts a byte stream into messages (type byte, 4-byte length, body) whatever the fragmentation, down to one byte at a time; also the untyped packets before startup. Enforces a maximum message size and refuses an oversized message from its header alone. Can skip the bodies of chosen message types instead of buffering them.

elements.name: Message coding
elements.description: Ours, written by hand, no pgproto3. Appends each message the session machines write (TLS and startup packets, authentication, parameter status, key data, ready, query, terminate, cancel) and parses the startup packet and its parameters.

elements.name: Codec boundary
elements.description: The only product code that may touch pgproto3: message structs encoded and decoded in one place. pgproto3's own blocking reader is not used. Nothing passes through it so far: the session machines, the trackers and the reply builders all use the hand-written message coding.

elements.name: Client session machine
elements.description: Client-facing, startup only: events in, actions out. Runs the exchange before startup: answers a TLS request S or N by client_tls.mode and asks its driver to start TLS (at most one upgrade; a byte before the handshake result is a violation), answers a GSS encryption request N. Reads the startup message, refuses plaintext when TLS is required, negotiates protocol 3.x down to 3.0, finds the tenant by user, runs SCRAM-SHA-256 (server side; trust only as a named test setting; an unknown user gets the wrong-password reply), sends the parameter set and proxy-issued key data, recognises cancel requests. Every failed startup ends under one reason. Consumes no byte after ready.

elements.name: Database session machine
elements.description: Database-facing, startup only: events in, actions out. Sends a TLS request first when backend_tls.mode asks for one (an N answer is a connect failure; a byte after S before the handshake result is a violation), then startup, SCRAM-SHA-256 (client side, never -PLUS), collects server parameters and key data, reaches ready. Every failed startup ends in one class (TLS refused or failed, authentication, too many connections, server FATAL, violation, deadline, connection lost).

elements.name: Query-cycle tracker
elements.description: Follows a reply to its ReadyForQuery, reports the transaction status byte (idle, in transaction, failed), flags an unsolicited ParameterStatus (the connection is now dirty) and any protocol surprise, including a stream that ends without its marker. Never buffers row data. Unknown but well-framed message types are reported and passed through.

elements.name: Client query-phase tracker
elements.description: Reads the client's bytes after login. Reports each Query (body copied, bounded), Terminate, and every extended-protocol message as one to refuse; any other message type is a violation.

elements.name: SCRAM-SHA-256 functions
elements.description: Pure functions on the standard library: verifier, key derivation, nonce, the GS2 header rule, and the server and client sides of the exchange with bounded messages. Shared with the simulator's fake Postgres and simulated clients.

elements.name: Startup FATAL replies
elements.description: The replies the session machines make themselves during startup: an ErrorResponse with severity, SQLSTATE and message, the old-format error for a protocol 2 client, and NegotiateProtocolVersion. Also parses the severity and SQLSTATE of an ErrorResponse from the database. The error table lists the startup rows too, but the session machines still build their replies here.

elements.name: Wire snapshot
elements.description: The wire layer's counters as one plain struct, per side: startups begun, completed, in progress and failed by reason; pre-startup requests by kind and answer; TLS handshakes by version and failure; plaintext refused; authentication failures by cause; messages and bytes each way; violations; oversized messages; what the trackers saw. Its check: begun = completed + failed + in startup, on each side.

elements.name: SQL lexer
elements.description: Tokens only: words, quoted and Unicode identifiers, strings (escape, Unicode and bit strings, and a string continued across a newline, joined as Postgres does), dollar quotes, numbers, parameters, operators, punctuation, comments; anything else is a bad token. Not a parser. Linear time.

elements.name: Reject list
elements.description: The courtesy list as one table: 16 reasons, each with the feature, why it cannot work under transaction pooling and an example, plus the transaction-scoped forms that are allowed. docs/reject-list.md is generated from it. Not a safety mechanism: no guarantee rests on it.

elements.name: Statement classifier
elements.description: Turns one Query message into a work unit. Lexes it, splits it on semicolons and rejects the whole message when any statement uses a reject-list feature (first reason wins); otherwise the unit starts a lease, or continues one inside a transaction. Never refuses a message for being untokenisable: it is marked opaque and forwarded. Sets safe-read from the safe-shape recogniser, shareable (safe-read, outside a transaction, not rejected), hinted (the text begins with /* mg:share */) and the share key (exact text, tenant by config). Counts by class and reason in its own snapshot, with a conservation check.

elements.name: Safe-shape recogniser
elements.description: Decides what may be shared, from the raw bytes alone: it uses neither the lexer nor the classifier and imports nothing. A text fits when it is at most 4,096 bytes of a small alphabet, starts with SELECT, has no word on the stop list, no time word in a string, and calls only functions on the allow-list. Allocates nothing. docs/safe-shape.md is generated from its tables. Stated limit: it cannot see a view, operator or row-level security policy that hides a side effect.

elements.name: Error contract and reply builders
elements.description: One table of 20 rows: each refusal and failure, its reply form, its SQLSTATE, whether anything reached the database, whether a write may have applied, and what happens to the client connection. The reply builder appends the ErrorResponse and the correct end marker for a row and counts replies by row. The discard-until-Sync rule refuses extended-protocol messages. docs/error-contract.md is generated from the table. Later chunks start to send their rows; so far only the two unsupported rows are sent, by the test gateway.

elements.name: Startup-only test proxy and startup fidelity runner
elements.description: internal/pgwire/pgwiretest. A proxy for tests on simulated streams: the two session machines back to back, one database connection per client, no pool; after login it relays queries and replies through both trackers. A database startup failure reaches the client as FATAL 08006. Also the startup fidelity runner: one script (TLS answers, SCRAM, protocol versions) played against the fake Postgres and compared with Postgres 17's transcript, recorded for CI or live in tier R.

elements.name: Wire scenarios
elements.description: internal/pgwire/pgwiretest/wireworld. 19 named scenarios with their exact checks: the test proxy between simulated clients and the fake Postgres, plaintext and TLS, one-byte delivery, and one startup fault each on the client side (TLS stall, bad hello, smuggled bytes, second TLS request, plaintext refused, wrong password, unknown user) or the database side (silence, connect stall, garbage, reset, connection limit, TLS refused, bad certificate, handshake stall). Each failure must be counted under its one reason within its deadline.

elements.name: Classifier scenarios
elements.description: internal/pgwire/pgwiretest/clsworld. Two named scenarios and a small test gateway on simulated streams: it relays startup to the fake Postgres (trust login, no session machines), classifies each Query, answers a rejected one and every extended-protocol message itself, and forwards the rest. Simulated clients send every reject-list feature, plain and in padded spellings. Checks: each gets 0A000, no rejected statement reaches the fake, and the session's search_path is unchanged.

elements.name: Rate gate (GCRA)
elements.description: Optional outer gate, off by default: a per-tenant rate and burst in integer nanoseconds. Refuses before anything is queued. Rates are divided by the instance count.

elements.name: Tenant table
elements.description: State for tenants that are active now: queue, in-flight count, share, gate state. Created on first use, removed when all-zero, so memory follows active tenants.

elements.name: Per-tenant queues
elements.description: A fixed-capacity ring per tenant. Age is measured on the oldest item; expired items are swept from the head and answered at once; overflow sheds the head. Serves newest-first while the rule reports overload (adaptive LIFO).

elements.name: QueueRule
elements.description: The interface both shedding rules implement; chosen by config.

elements.name: Timeout rule
elements.description: Mode 1, from "Fail at Scale": one last-empty timestamp per queue; allowed wait is the short target while a standing queue exists, otherwise the interval.

elements.name: Control-law rule
elements.description: Mode 2, from the CoDel paper and RFC 8289: sojourn above target for an interval starts dropping; next drop after interval / sqrt(count), in integer arithmetic.

elements.name: Comparison arms
elements.description: Simulator only: plain FIFO and folly's minimum-delay detector, for the head-to-head table.

elements.name: Dispatcher
elements.description: Chooses whose request runs next: round robin across tenants with waiting work; a tenant's share binds only when the limit is reached; otherwise work-conserving.

elements.name: Adaptive limit (AIMD)
elements.description: One integer limit on concurrent leases. Cut by a tenth on a slow statement, a timeout or a connection failure; raised by one when busy. Bounded by a floor, the pool size, a maximum step and a minimum interval. Reads database round-trip time, never queue wait.

elements.name: Admission snapshot
elements.description: Snapshot(): per tenant and total — depth, oldest-item age, queue-wait histogram, rule state, LIFO switches, sheds by reason, in flight, share, limit and its changes, gate refusals.

elements.name: Connection accounting
elements.description: Every database connection is connecting, idle, lent or closing. Invariant: open + connecting never exceeds the pool size, which is the fleet budget divided by the instance count.

elements.name: Creation limiter
elements.description: Caps concurrent connects and the rate of new connections, so a storm or a cold start cannot flood the database.

elements.name: Lease table
elements.description: Lends a connection for one transaction: held while the status byte says in-transaction or failed, released on idle. Enforces the idle-in-transaction deadline.

elements.name: Database-down breaker
elements.description: The one circuit breaker. Counts connection-class failures only, never SQL errors. Open: requests are refused at once and no dial is made. Half-open: one trial connect.

elements.name: Dirty-connection table
elements.description: What to do with a connection whose client vanished or that surprised us: cancel, wait a bounded time, roll back, then reuse only if it is idle and clean; otherwise close. Destroy on doubt.

elements.name: Idle and lifetime reaper
elements.description: Closes idle and old connections, with jitter so they do not all expire together; checks a long-idle connection before reuse.

elements.name: Cancel map
elements.description: Maps proxy-issued key data to the connection a client currently holds, so a client's cancel request reaches its own statement and no one else's. Caps concurrent cancels.

elements.name: Pool snapshot
elements.description: Snapshot(): open, idle, lent, connecting, creation rate, closes by reason, exhaustion events, breaker state and transitions, dirty-table outcomes, lease-time histogram.

elements.name: Join rule
elements.description: Decides whether a shareable request leads a new read or joins one. Strict (default): never join a read already running on the database — join the next one, which starts when the running one ends. Relaxed: join the running read.

elements.name: Flight table
elements.description: In-flight and pending shared reads, keyed by the exact statement text. At most one read per key is on the database at a time. Entries are removed on completion.

elements.name: Waiter set
elements.description: The callers of one flight, counted. Capped. A caller that leaves gets its own error and does not disturb the rest.

elements.name: Flight deadline
elements.description: The flight runs under its own deadline, not any caller's. The database work is cancelled only when the last waiter has left.

elements.name: Shared reply buffer
elements.description: The reply's message bytes, stored once and capped; each recipient gets them with its own end marker. Errors are shared too.

elements.name: Do-not-share list
elements.description: Keys whose reply was too large to share. Bounded and expiring.

elements.name: Coalescer snapshot
elements.description: Snapshot(): flights, hits, waiters per flight, cancellations, overflows by cap, shared errors, table size.

elements.name: Policy
elements.description: The interface the engine asks: given this failure — did anything reach the database, is the breaker open, how much of the deadline is left — may it be retried.

elements.name: Off
elements.description: The default. Never retries.

elements.name: PreForwardOnce
elements.description: Retries at most once, only when nothing reached the database, only within budget, never while the breaker is open, never holding a queue slot or a connection while it waits.

elements.name: Retry budget
elements.description: An integer bucket: each first attempt deposits a tenth of a token, each retry takes one; capped, so credit expires. Retries stay at or below 10% of requests.

elements.name: Retry snapshot
elements.description: Snapshot(): attempts, retries, budget level, deposits, withdrawals, exhaustions, refusals by reason.

elements.name: Event loop
elements.description: internal/sim. One thread, one heap ordered by (time, sequence). An event is a closure, or an opaque handler with an integer code. Step, run until a time, run until quiet. A step budget, typed stall errors (budget spent, time frozen, heap full) and a panic guard, each carrying the REPLAY line.

elements.name: Virtual clock and timers
elements.description: internal/sim. 64-bit nanoseconds that saturate instead of overflowing. Cancellable timers: a cancel removes the event from the heap. A timer marked background does not count in the quiesce check. Time moves only when the loop moves it.

elements.name: Named random streams
elements.description: internal/sim. One generator per (seed, label), so a new draw in one place does not shift any other.

elements.name: Simulated byte streams
elements.description: internal/sim/simnet. Listeners and ordered byte connections with chosen fragmentation (down to one byte), latency per direction, a bounded send window (back pressure), half-close and reset. Its faults: reset, stall, half-open, half-close, chunk, refuse, dial stall, accept-then-silence, and clear. Its own snapshot.

elements.name: Fake Postgres
elements.description: internal/sim/fakepg. Speaks the simple-query subset in real wire bytes with its own framer; login by trust or SCRAM-SHA-256; answers a TLS request S or N and plays the simulated handshake; a max_connections limit with Postgres's refusal; transaction status; a small keyed table with write, statement and transaction logs; service-time models and a capacity limit; cancel requests; every database-side fault (the TLS ones — answers N, a handshake that fails or stalls, a certificate that fails verification — are a setting that can change during a run, not fault kinds); its own snapshots.

elements.name: Clients and tenants
elements.description: internal/sim/workload. Simulated clients grouped in tenants: open-loop arrivals (constant or Poisson) and closed-loop think time, latency measured from the intended send time, uniform, Zipf or fixed keys, transactions of several statements, retries with backoff; login by trust or SCRAM-SHA-256, with a TLS request first when the tenant asks; every client-side fault (the four TLS ones — stall after the request, bad hello, plaintext after the request, a second request — are a per-tenant setting); its own snapshot. A client sends one request at a time; later arrivals wait in its bounded backlog. Also a hand-driven client (Probe) for tests.

elements.name: Test client
elements.description: internal/testclient. A Postgres client with no I/O: bytes in, messages out. Its own framer, a message codec, and a session machine (phase, status byte, key data, parameters) with trust login. It hands the data of each authentication message to its caller, which is how the simulated clients run SCRAM. Used by the simulated clients on simulated streams and by the tier R tests on TCP.

elements.name: Simulated TLS handshake
elements.description: internal/sim/simtls. A handshake as an exchange with an outcome, not cryptography: a 16-byte client hello (or a bad one) and a 16-byte server reply that says completed with a TLS version, bad certificate, or alert. Models the outcome and the duration only.

elements.name: Float generators
elements.description: internal/randdist. The only two functions that use floating point: exponential gaps for Poisson arrivals, and a Zipf generator. Kept outside internal/sim, where float syntax is forbidden.

elements.name: Scenario world
elements.description: internal/sim/world. The scenario type; the driver interface (start, connect, inject, run, observe, stop) and its simulator implementation; five direct baselines with no proxy (500 connections, reconnect burst, 1,000 identical reads, open-loop overload, mixed transactions); the write-log and transaction checks; the fidelity runner, which plays one script against the fake and compares the transcript with Postgres 17's, recorded for CI or live in tier R.

elements.name: Fault schedule and shrinker
elements.description: internal/sim. Timed faults, each recorded in the trace when it is applied. A package registers the fault kinds it can apply. A schedule can be decoded from bytes for the fuzzer, and a delete-one-fault shrinker cuts a failing schedule down. Faults are injected only from outside the code under test.

elements.name: Decision trace and digests
elements.description: internal/sim. Any actor appends a record (time, kind, four integers) in order; the last records are kept in a ring for failure reports. Two digests: one of the trace, one of final state as written by registered state writers. Same seed, same digests.

elements.name: Invariants and quiesce check
elements.description: internal/sim. A package registers its checks. Invariants run after every event (or every Nth); the quiesce checks run at the end of a run: nothing in use, nothing in flight, no timer left. A failed check fails the run.

elements.name: Seeds, replay, sweep
elements.description: internal/sim/simtest. The seed flag and variables, pinned seeds, the sweep over seeds, the run-twice check, the failure report with the trace tail and the REPLAY line. scripts/sweep.sh and scripts/fuzz.sh run the scenario tests and fuzz targets through it.

elements.name: cmd/mgsim
elements.description: Lists the named scenarios (toy and world); runs one from a seed outside go test, prints its digests (and the trace on request; for a world scenario also its result table) and exits 1 with the REPLAY line when it fails.

elements.name: Toy echo protocol
elements.description: internal/sim/simtoy. A line-echo client and server with a planted-bug switch, and eleven named scenarios that cover every network fault. Used only to test the harness itself.

elements.name: Snapshot conventions
elements.description: The one common raw export. What every component's Snapshot() returns: a plain struct of monotonic counters and current gauges. No wall-clock time, no map order, no telemetry imports. Nothing else leaves a component; an import rule keeps components and the simulator from importing any adapter.

elements.name: Integer histogram
elements.description: Fixed array, fixed relative error, no allocation on record; record, merge, percentile. Out-of-range values are clamped and counted.

elements.name: Conservation check and gauge
elements.description: A check that a total equals the sum of its parts (for example written = delivered + discarded + in flight); its error names each term and which side is higher. A gauge type that keeps a value and its peak.

elements.name: Snapshot and adapter test helpers
elements.description: internal/obs/obstest. Test plumbing: checks that a snapshot is a plain struct of integers (no time, no map), and that every counter in it moved in at least one test. Also the conformance test every adapter must pass (values, labels, determinism, no kept reference, errors counted), its shared fixture, and the golden-file helper.

elements.name: Metric registry
elements.description: Every exported metric is declared first: component, name, kind (counter, gauge, histogram), which of the four labels it has (tenant, outcome, reason, mode), unit, merge rule (sum, or max for a high-water mark), and whether it is a headline metric. Refuses a bad or repeated name and names that would clash in Prometheus.

elements.name: Instance snapshot
elements.description: What the collector publishes and all an adapter gets: instance id, build, config fingerprint, publish sequence number, and sorted lists of points (integer values) and histogram points. No time, no map.

elements.name: Detail gate
elements.description: The obs.detail setting. Off: the collector folds every tenant into one and drops histogram points, and a detail histogram holds no buckets (a record is one nil check). On: per-tenant rows and full histograms.

elements.name: Collector
elements.description: Components register as sources: their metric declarations, their Snapshot and a mapping from it to points. At each publish it assembles one instance snapshot (with instance id, build and config fingerprint), refusing an undeclared, mistyped, duplicate or missing metric, and hands it to every attached adapter. Keeps the last published snapshot and gives out copies. Counts its own work (publishes, emit errors, export errors per adapter, CSV flushes and drops) as component obs. The only path from a component snapshot to an adapter.

elements.name: Adapter interface
elements.description: The one interface every output form implements: a name, and take the published instance snapshot and produce output. A failed export is counted by the collector and never reaches the publisher. One conformance test for all adapters. Components cannot see past it, so none knows about CSV, DuckDB, OTel or Prometheus.

elements.name: Fleet merge
elements.description: Merges instance snapshots: each metric by its declared rule (sum, or max for a high-water mark), histograms bucket by bucket. Refuses an undeclared metric, a kind or unit clash and an integer overflow. Ratios are never stored, so they are recomputed from the merged counts, never averaged.

elements.name: Health
elements.description: Three states, the worst over a table of named rules, with a reason per rule and a JSON body. The collector rule: degraded before the first publish, and while the latest publish had metric errors or an adapter's export failed. Other rules: degraded while shedding, while the breaker is open, at the limit's floor, or draining; failed only when this instance cannot work. A database outage is degraded.
plannedNotes: Built in chunk 3 (internal/obs: health.go): the three states, the rule table (overall state is the worst rule), the collector rule and the JSON body. Not built: the rules for shedding, an open breaker, the limit's floor, draining and a database outage, and any rule that gives failed (chunk 6 on).

elements.name: Prometheus text exporter
elements.description: internal/obs/promtext. Names mg_<component>_<metric>, low-cardinality labels and a bounded tenant label: configured tenants, or the first active ones, up to a cap; quiet tenants lose their slot; the rest are summed as other. Histograms are re-bucketed onto a short bound list. Holds the exposition-grammar checker the tests use.

elements.name: JSON stats exporter
elements.description: internal/obs/jsonstats. The full snapshot, including every active tenant; it decodes back to an equal snapshot.

elements.name: CSV flush adapter
elements.description: internal/obs/csvflush. Flushes snapshots to disk at each publish and at the end of a run, in a stable versioned schema with unbounded per-tenant rows. The testing path: tests assert on the files with no Collector or Prometheus running. Bounded size; drop-and-count at the cap, on a write error and on a full queue. Writes in the caller (simulator and tests) or through a bounded queue that never blocks the caller (real process). Holds the reader and the round-trip check: the final flush read back equals the snapshot.

elements.name: Log-line exporter
elements.description: internal/obs/logline. One structured line per publish: sequence number, instance, build, config fingerprint and the headline metrics. At most 1,024 bytes.

elements.name: OTLP/HTTP push exporter
elements.description: The final adapter and the proxy's end of the production path. Hand-written on the standard library, no SDK. Cumulative sums, gauges, short-list histogram buckets, bounded tenant label. Bounded queue, timeout, drop-and-count when the Collector is down. Lands in the last build chunk and touches no component.

elements.name: Simulator source mappings
elements.description: internal/obs/simsrc. The metric declarations and the snapshot-to-points mappings of the four simulator components that exist: the kernel, simnet, the fake Postgres (its authentication and TLS counters too) and the workload (its startup counters too). It lives here because the simulator packages are frozen; a later component writes the same two functions in its own package.

elements.name: Wire source mapping
elements.description: internal/obs/wiresrc. The metric declarations of component wire and the mapping from the wire snapshot to points. The side is in the metric name (client_..., database_...); labels are reason, outcome and mode; every known label value is emitted, zero included; no tenant label.

elements.name: Classifier source mapping
elements.description: internal/obs/clssrc. The metric declarations of component classifier and the mapping to points from three wire-layer snapshots: the classifier's (statements, by class, rejects by reason, opaque, safe-read, shareable, hinted, share keys), the reply builder's (replies by error-table row, failures) and the discard-until-Sync counters. All counters; every known label value is emitted, zero included; no tenant label.

elements.name: Metric catalog and schema document
elements.description: internal/obs/catalog. The registry of every source the product registers, and the generator of docs/csv-schema.md (columns of the three files and every metric). Its test fails when the committed document differs from the code; scripts/gen-docs.sh regenerates or checks it.

elements.name: Scenario flush harness
elements.description: internal/obs/simrun. Runs a simulator world scenario, a wire scenario or a classifier scenario, with a collector that publishes on the virtual clock and with the CSV, JSON, Prometheus and log adapters attached, then checks every output against the final snapshot. Its tests run the five direct baselines, every wire scenario and both classifier scenarios twice per seed and compare the files byte for byte.

elements.name: SQL assertions and their runner
elements.description: scripts/csv-assert.sh and test/analysis. The runner finds run directories, checks them with guard.sql (schema version, no empty required field, one run id per directory, no empty run), loads views.sql and runs each assertion file; a returned row is a violation. Fails closed and never skips. The assertion files check the direct baselines' counts and, for each wire scenario, that startup failures by reason, TLS requests by answer and handshake failures equal what was injected and sent, and for the classifier scenarios that rejects equal the statements sent and the fake Postgres started only what was forwarded (nothing in the reject-only scenario).

elements.name: Application hosts
elements.description: Clients of every tenant. They spread their connections over the instances themselves, or through any TCP balancer; we build none.

elements.name: Proxy tier, N = 3
elements.description: Three independent mini-gateway processes with the same static config: fleet.instances = 3, so each takes a third of every fleet budget. No instance knows about the others.

elements.name: Database host
elements.description: One Postgres. Its connection limit must cover the fleet budget plus a reserve; config validation checks it.

elements.name: Operations
elements.description: Where metrics are scraped or pushed to, and merged across instances.

elements.name: Client connections
elements.description: 500 clients here; each connects to one instance.

elements.name: mini-gateway instance 1
elements.description: Own engine, pool (fleet budget / 3), queues, flights, limit, retry budget and snapshots. Drains on SIGTERM.

elements.name: mini-gateway instance 2
elements.description: Own engine, pool (fleet budget / 3), queues, flights, limit, retry budget and snapshots. Drains on SIGTERM.

elements.name: mini-gateway instance 3
elements.description: Own engine, pool (fleet budget / 3), queues, flights, limit, retry budget and snapshots. Drains on SIGTERM.

elements.name: Postgres 17
elements.description: Sees at most the fleet connection budget (for example 3 x 32 = 96), all as one role.

elements.name: Scraper or collector
elements.description: Reads each instance's exporters; sums counters, merges histograms, recomputes ratios.
